clause_text_ref.legal: Regulation (EU) 2023/1230 (CELEX 32023R1230), Annex IV, Part A, point (g)

regulation_clauses.route: Internal production control (module A, Art. 25(4) and Annex VI) against the Annex III essential health and safety requirements; no notified body. Annex I, Part A, points 5 and 6 concern machine learning that both ensures a safety function and is fully or partially self-evolving (recital 55); this is a frozen task policy. Applies from 20 January 2027 (Art. 54, as corrected); Directive 2006/42/EC until then.
regulation_clauses.why: Results of tests on the control logic: the task, the success definition signed before the results, the seeds, per-scenario verdicts and the trace.
regulation_clauses.not_shown: Which essential health and safety requirement each test verifies (the manufacturer's risk assessment, Part A (b), makes that link); tests on the physical machine.

task.success_definition: gym_aloha/env.py AlohaEnv.step: `terminated = is_success = reward == 4`. gym_aloha/tasks/sim.py TransferCubeTask.get_reward, from contact pairs: 1 = cube touches the right gripper finger; 2 = and not the table (lifted); 3 = cube touches the left gripper finger (attempted transfer); 4 = left finger and not the table (successful transfer). max_reward = 4.

policy.derivation: lerobot 0.6.1 `python -m lerobot.processor.migrate_policy_normalization --pretrained-path <original> --output-dir <migrated>`, run offline (HF_HUB_OFFLINE=1) on the published revision, which moves the normalisation statistics out of the weights into processor files; then the device fields in config.json and policy_preprocessor.json are set to "cpu", the device inference runs on. Without that second step the migration writes whatever accelerator the deriving host auto-selects in place of the published "cuda" (measured: "mps" on macos-arm64, "cpu" on linux-x86_64), so the derived files differed by platform
